extracted.intended_audience: trademark applicants, trademark attorneys, and TTAB practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements for filing, publishing, and litigating U.S. trademark concurrent use registration applications before the Trademark Trial and Appeal Board (TTAB), including when a new concurrent use proceeding is required or may be avoided based on prior Board or court determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of a concurrent use application (37 C.F.R. § 2.42)
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must state the area, goods and/or services, and (if applicable) mode of use for which applicant seeks registration, and must state, to the extent of applicant's knowledge, the concurrent lawful use of the mark by others, setting forth their names and addresses, their areas of use, the goods and/or services on or in connection with which their use is made, the mode of their use, the periods of their use, and the registrations issued to or applications filed by them, if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should provide full detail about geographic area, goods/services, and mode of use sought; and as to other users, list names/addresses/areas/goods/mode/periods/registrations or applications. See 37 C.F.R. § 2.42 and TBMP § 1103.01(c)-(f). Submission of required elements avoids processing delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to list known senior users and junior users with clearly established rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant need not list every entity known to be using the same or similar mark, but must list any entity known to it to be a senior user of a clearly conflicting mark and any junior user known to have clearly established rights (e.g., by court decree, settlement agreement, or registration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not omit known senior users or junior users whose rights are 'clearly established.' The duty to investigate extends to known prior users; there is no requirement to report every possible user. Case citations: Rosso & Mastracco, Pennsylvania Fashion Factory, In re Sun Refining & Marketing Co., SCOA Industries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking and publication when application is subject to a concurrent use proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: When approved for publication, an application entitled to registration subject to a concurrent use proceeding is marked: 'SUBJECT TO CONCURRENT USE PROCEEDING WITH _______________. APPLICANT CLAIMS EXCLUSIVE RIGHT TO USE THE MARK IN THE AREA COMPRISING ________________.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first blank fills with involved application/registration numbers or names/addresses if no registration; the second blank with the geographic area and any limitations. If application is based on a prior Board decision and a new proceeding is unnecessary, it is instead marked: 'REGISTRATION LIMITED TO THE AREA COMPRISING ______________ PURSUANT TO CONCURRENT USE PROCEEDING NO. _______. CONCURRENT REGISTRATION WITH ______________.' The Board will publish in the Official Gazette and send notices (including web links) to applicant and excepted users (37 C.F.R. §§ 2.80, 2.99(b)-(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions to avoid a new concurrent use proceeding when relying on a prior Board decision
rubrics_metrics.description: A new concurrent use proceeding will not be instituted if: (1) the applicant is entitled to registration subject only to the concurrent lawful use of a party or parties to the prior proceeding; (2) the Board’s prior decision specifies applicant's right to concurrent registration; (3) a copy of the Board’s prior decision is submitted to the examining attorney; (4) the concurrent use application complies with the Board’s prior decision (seeks same or more limited geographic area or mode of use, same or less confusingly similar mark, and substantially the same or more limited goods/services); and (5) the excepted use specified does not involve a registration, or any involved registration has been restricted in accordance with the Board’s prior decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any condition fails, a new concurrent use proceeding will be instituted. If conditions (1)-(4) are met but involved registration was not restricted per the prior decision, a proceeding will be instituted solely to restrict that registration; if no good cause is shown, the registration is restricted and the applicant is found entitled to the registration. Legal effect invoked: res judicata and stare decisis when conditions are met. See TBMP § 1103.02 and related notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions to avoid a concurrent use proceeding when relying on a court decree (37 C.F.R. § 2.99(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: A concurrent use registration proceeding will not be instituted when: (1) the applicant is entitled to registration subject only to the concurrent lawful use of a party to the court proceeding; (2) the court decree specifies the rights of the parties; (3) a true copy of the court decree is submitted to the examining attorney; (4) the concurrent use application complies fully and exactly with the court decree; and (5) the excepted use specified does not involve a registration, or if it does, the involved registration has been restricted by the Director in accordance with the court decree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application based on a court determination must assert use in commerce of the mark sought to be registered and must comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 2.42 elements. NOTE: such an application need not meet the jurisdictional requirement of use in commerce prior to the date in Trademark Act § 2(d), nor must it satisfy the Director that confusion is unlikely; issuance on the basis of a court decree is independent of those provisions. If conditions are not satisfied, a concurrent use proceeding is instituted (or instituted solely to restrict registrations if appropriate). See TBMP § 1103.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who are parties to a concurrent use proceeding and amendment to parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties are the concurrent use applicant(s) and all persons listed in the application as exceptions (excepted users), who may be applicants, registrants, or common law users. Often proceedings involve the concurrent use applicant and a common law user without involved registration or application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If after commencement the applicant learns of another person with conflicting rights, the applicant may move to amend the application to list that person; if granted, that person is added and notified. If a listed excepted user abandons the mark or assigns it to applicant, applicant may move to delete that person; motions should include factual explanations. See TBMP § 1104 and notes (Gallagher’s Restaurants, Fleming Companies, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Which applications and registrations are 'involved' and how unpublished/conflicting applications are treated
rubrics_metrics.description: Involved applications/registrations include the concurrent use application(s); every conflicting unrestricted application identified in the concurrent use application(s) that was filed prior to the concurrent use filing date; registrations identified in the concurrent use application(s) as being owned by listed exceptions; and every registration claimed by the concurrent use applicant unless there is no conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an identified application has not yet been published or cleared opposition, it is included as a common law user rather than an applicant; the Board may suspend the proceeding until the unpublished application is abandoned or published and survives opposition and then add it. The Board inquires whether parties own other conflicting apps/regs and will add them where appropriate. If a party owns a conflicting unrestricted application filed after the concurrent use application, the examining attorney will suspend action on that subsequent unrestricted application pending disposition of the concurrent use application; if the concurrent use application matures, it will be cited under § 2(d) against the subsequent unrestricted application. If the later-filed applicant amends to seek concurrent registration and it clears publication without opposition, it may be added to the proceeding. See TBMP § 1104 and notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of issues properly before the Board in a concurrent use proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: The only issue properly before the Board concerns the concurrent use applicant’s entitlement to registration. The specific territorial rights of common law users are not before the Board except insofar as those rights may limit the registration rights to which applicant proves entitlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common law users who do not own involved applications or registrations cannot have their registration rights determined in the proceeding; they must file their own application seeking concurrent registration and, if instituted, a concurrent use proceeding will determine their rights. See TBMP § 1104.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications and registrations not subject to concurrent use proceedings; intent-to-use handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications/registrations on the Supplemental Register and registrations under the Act of 1920 are not subject to concurrent use proceedings. Applications based solely on Trademark Act §§ 44 or 66(a) are not subject. Intent-to-use applications under § 1(b) are subject only after filing an acceptable allegation of use under 37 C.F.R. § 2.76 or § 2.88. An application that includes § 1(a) as a filing basis, or for which an acceptable allegation under § 2.76/2.88 has been filed, may be amended to seek concurrent use registration if it meets § 2.42 requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may not amend an intent-to-use application to seek concurrent use until use is effected; amendments to allege use cannot be filed after the application has been approved for publication. Applications are in a 'blackout period' while an opposition is pending. If parties wish concurrent registrations, an applicant may consider abandoning an opposed application and refiling as a use-based concurrent use application (with opposer's consent to avoid judgment). Opposers may consider amending their pending applications to seek concurrent use to permit full adjudication. See 37 C.F.R. § 2.73, 2.99(g), TBMP § 1103.01(a) and notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of incontestable registrations in concurrent use proceedings and tolling of incontestability
rubrics_metrics.description: An incontestable registration (under Trademark Act § 15) is subject to a concurrent use proceeding; however, any registration issued to the concurrent use applicant as against the owner of an incontestable registration will be limited to the applicant’s area of actual use prior to actual or constructive notice of the registrant’s rights, unless the parties stipulate otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The five-year incontestability period for a registration is tolled with respect to an applicant’s concurrent rights if, prior to expiration of the five-year period, the applicant files a proper concurrent use application (or an amendment converting an unrestricted application into one seeking concurrent use). Case citations include Boi Na Braza, Holiday Inn, Thriftimart, and Arman’s Systems. See TBMP § 1105 and notes.
